one_month_reasoning: No CoreWeave earnings fall inside Oct 2-31. StockAnalysis estimates Q3 results for Nov 9, 2026, which is not confirmed, and Q3 2025 was reported Nov 10. In-window movers: (1) supply from the new ATM program (up to 35M shares) and steady insider Form 144/Form 4 sales, a mild headwind; (2) hedging flows around the new 2033 converts ($97.85 conversion); (3) AI-capex read-throughs from hyperscaler Q3 earnings around Oct 28-29 (estimated dates), which could go either way; (4) the FOMC on Oct 27-28; (5) credit headlines, since CDS moved from 452bp (June) to ~855bp (July) to ~811bp (Sept), and the equity trades with it. Alt-data shows no stress: OCPI H100 rose from $2.71 to $2.92, older-gen rental rates rose through 2026, and hiring is steady at 311 open roles. Round 3 adds one in-window item: CME/Silicon Data compute futures launch on Oct 5, which will publish the first exchange forward curve for GPU-hour prices; a steeply backwardated curve would be read as the market pricing the GPU-value decay my DCF now models, so it is a two-sided headline risk rather than a directional call. The GPU-life rebuild and the SBC correction change long-run value, not the next 30 days, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged. Round 4's site and discount-rate work also changes long-run value only; the in-window site items (PF1 Building 2's last 75 MW on Oct 2, and Cheyenne/Calgary toward the YE26 guide) are small: a near-symmetric lognormal with median ~$88 (slightly below spot for ATM supply) and 26% monthly vol (93%/3.5).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a site-bucketed GPU-cohort DCF ($1.0/sh with contracted cash flows at a split rate; $0.8 at one 11.6% WACC) and 6.0x Oct-27 NTM adj. EBITDA of $19.1B less $63.0B net debt incl. JV commitments ($81.9/sh). The DCF now values each site once: 1.85 GW energized and 2.44 GW contracted capacity (delivery-probability weighted, avg p 0.86) are worth ~$72/sh of EV, the uncontracted pipeline is negative (-$15/sh) at k 2.6, and net debt of ~$98/sh leaves an unfloored central case of -$42; the floored regime x k expectation is $1.0.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued at 2027-10-01. Round-3 GPU-cohort engine unchanged (85% of each cohort priced at contract for 5 yrs, then shortage 0.30 / normalising 0.50 / glut 0.20 repricing x 0.92 utilisation; 30% capacity-tied + 12% variable cost; cash tail; 6-yr tech refresh at 0.83k with 10% salvage; DC at 15 yrs; SBC 5%->3%; tax 0% to 2028 then 21% after $6B NOL; k grid 2.3/2.6/2.7 at 0.25/0.5/0.25). New in round 4: (1) the nameplate path is built from the site inventory: E = 1,850 MW energized by YE26 at $10M/MW-yr ($18.5B), C = 2,435 MW contracted-not-energized (4.2 GW + Niagara 85 MW - E) at $11M/MW-yr, each site weighted by its delivery probability (expected 2,098 MW), then PIPE-LAND (1,415 MW, p 0.65) and the residual to the round-3 $76B 2036 path (p 0.35), all net of growth capex at k. Path: 2027 $26.3B, 2028 35.3, 2029 43.3, 2030 48.5, 2031 52.1, 2036 57.0 (round 3: 38, 48, 56, 62, 76). (2) Split discounting: the $77.1B of RPO left at 2027-10-01 (10-Q: 41% in months 1-24, 39% in 25-48, 20% in 49-78), net of 58% EBITDA margin, SBC and tax, is discounted by counterparty: IG 52% at 7.0% (DDTL 4.0 A3 secured cost ~5.9% + ~110bp completion/operating), Jane Street 6% at 8.0%, OpenAI/Anthropic 23% at 9.0% (DDTL 3.0 S+400), other/short-dated 19% at 10.0% (S+450-550); PV-equivalent 8.06%. Everything else (post-contract, unsigned future contracts, refresh cohorts, pipeline, terminal) stays at the 11.6% WACC. Uplift +$2.0B (+$3.2/sh). (3) Net debt $61.6B + $1.37B JV commitments - $0.16B NJ EDA credit = $62.8B. Per share at k 2.6, 6 yrs, split (shortage / normalising / glut): -$20 / -$48 / -$62; at k 2.3: +$13 / -$15 / -$29. Floored expectation: $1.0 split ($0.76 single); 5/7/8-yr: $0.0 / $2.6 / $6.3. Unfloored central: -$42.3 split, -$45.5 single (round 3 -$53).

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $26.26B. It sits above the ~$24.5B straight line between the exit-2026 run-rate guide ($18.5-19.5B) and the exit-2027 target of >$30B.

Built bottom-up from sites.md: energized 1,850 MW (YE26 guide; 990 MW named + 88 MW Cheyenne + 772 MW undisclosed pool) at $10M/MW-yr (exit-2026 ARR $18.5-19.5B / 1.85 GW); contracted-not-energized 2,435 MW (named 1,671 MW + 764 MW unattributed) at $11M/MW-yr (consensus 2027 $26.3B on ~2.4 GW average), each weighted by its delivery probability (Helios II/PF1-B3/Lancaster/Dalton P2 0.95, Helios III 0.90, Kenilworth/Niagara/pool 0.85, Indonesia 0.80, Hammond 0.70); timing follows the round-3 path capped at the contracted $45.3B. Uncontracted: PIPE-LAND 1,415 MW x $11M at p 0.65 and the residual ~$15B to the round-3 $76B 2036 level at p 0.35. This fixes flags F6 ($7M/MW understated revenue per MW) and F7 (8 GW treated as certain).

inputs_detail.input: Adj. EBITDA margin at full contract price
inputs_detail.value: 58% (59% in 2027), split 30% capacity-tied cost on nameplate + 12% variable on revenue
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2'26: adj. EBITDA $1,510M on $2,575M (59%). Cost of revenue was $879M (34%; DC leases, power, data-center staff), and the other cash opex was ~7%. I put 30 pts of cost on in-service capacity, because leases and power do not fall when a GPU's price does, and 12 pts on revenue. At full price this reproduces round 2's 58%. When old cohorts reprice, EBITDA margin falls: 53-56% in 2030-36 in the normalising regime.

inputs_detail.input: SBC deducted as a cash cost
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor's round-2 correction: adj. EBITDA adds back SBC, which was $165M on $2,575M revenue in Q2'26 (6.4%) and $318M in H1 (8-K Ex.99.1, 10-Q). Unrecognised RSU expense is $1.7B over ~3 yrs (10-Q). Falling to 3% as revenue scales. It costs $28/sh on the round-2 model, more than the supervisor's $10-20 estimate, because 3% of a $70-80B revenue base is perpetual.

inputs_detail.value: 85% of each new cohort contracted for 5 yrs at the contract price; 15% on the market path
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: of $103.7B RPO, 41% is recognised within 24 months, 39% in months 25-48 and the rest in months 49-78, so the longest contracts run ~6.5 yrs and the weighted remaining term is ~2.6 yrs. On a book that is mostly 1-2 yrs old, that implies original terms of ~4-5 yrs. The 15% uncontracted covers the short 3-6 month contracts in the September commitments and on-demand capacity.

inputs_detail.input: Post-contract revenue path per GPU (relative to the original contract price)
inputs_detail.value: Regime-weighted: shortage 0.30 (0.95 at age 3, 0.90 at 5, 0.86 at 6), normalising 0.50 (0.78 at 3, 0.64 at 5, 0.59 at 6, 0.50 at 8), glut 0.20 (0.65 at 3, 0.52 at 5, 0.44 at 7); x 0.92 relative utilisation (0.95 shortage, 0.90 glut)
inputs_detail.derivation: Steep in the ~2 yrs after the next generation ships, flatter after. The H100 composite fell ~50% in ~18 months from its 2H23 on-demand level, then held ~$2.80 (SemiAnalysis). Contract prices start below on-demand, so the fall relative to the contract price is smaller: normalising is -36% by age 5. A100 still earns $0.93-1.58/hr at 6 yrs (Ornn, Silicon Data), 23-39% of on-demand launch and roughly half of a contract price. Ornn shows A100/H100/B200 at about the same ~$3 per PFLOP-hr, so old chips reprice with the cost of compute rather than to scrap, and Rubin's claimed 10x lower cost per token (CES) sets the pace of that repricing. Shortage weight: CoreWeave re-booked H100s within 5% (CNBC), signed an A100 contract into 2029 (Tom's Hardware) and AWS has never retired an A100. Only 0.30 because the research notes that all of this comes from a supply- and power-constrained market.

inputs_detail.value: Base 6 yrs: tech refreshed in the same MW at 0.83 x 2.6 per $ of nameplate; 5- and 7-yr sensitivities; DC equipment replaced at 15 yrs
inputs_detail.derivation: Base 6 = the 5-yr contract plus about one year of repriced tail, before the MW is worth more with a new generation (research [J]: years 5-6 are where a power slot is worth more re-filled). It matches CoreWeave's 6-yr book life (S-1). The research suggests 5 as the neocloud base; 5 is the downside case, given Amazon's 6->5 cut for AI servers and Kerrisdale's margin math. 7 is the upside case, given A100s still earning at 6-9 yrs. Physical/cash life runs longer: in the model a cohort would keep positive cash until ~age 9 (normalising), like V100 at break-even near 9 yrs. Refresh reuses the shell, so only the 83% tech share is re-spent (10-Q PP&E mix).

inputs_detail.value: 10% of tech cost at 6 yrs (14% at 5, 7% at 7, 4% at 8)
inputs_detail.derivation: CCIR executed medians: H100 35% of launch at 3.9 yrs, A100 80GB 21% at 5.8, A100 40GB 15% at 6.3, V100 3.5% at 8.5. GPUs are ~70% of server cost and selling costs are ~15%, so 21% x 0.7 x 0.85 = ~12% at 6 yrs, trimmed to 10% because resale prices also reflect today's shortage. CoreWeave books no salvage. Salvage is worth ~$13/sh at 7 yrs, so it is a material assumption.

inputs_detail.value: 0% through 2028; then 21% of EBIT (book D&A over 6 yrs) after a ~$6B NOL
inputs_detail.derivation: FY25 net loss $1.17B, H1'26 $1.37B, plus earlier losses, with a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets (call). The ~$6B NOL is a judgment from cumulative losses.

10-yr yield ~5.29% (Sept). Damodaran's Jan-2026 implied ERP of 4.23% replaces round 1's round 5%. Beta 2.0 is a judgment: 93% realized vol against ~16% market vol at ~0.35 correlation gives ~2.0 (StockAnalysis lists no 5-yr beta for this 2025 IPO).

inputs_detail.value: 9.0%, with no tax shield while NOLs shelter income
inputs_detail.derivation: Management says its weighted average cost of debt fell ~300bp in a year (call). The Q3 interest guide of $860-940M on ~$40B is ~9%. Contractual Q2 interest of $592M on a ~$32B average is ~7.4% (10-Q). Marginal unsecured coupons are 9-9.75% and DDTLs run at SOFR+2.25-4.5% (10-Q). Round 1's 11.5-12% came from press-relayed secondary yields in a stressed week (CDS swung from 452bp in June to 855bp in July), so it is not the marginal funding cost.

inputs_detail.value: 11.6% for uncontracted, post-contract, pipeline and terminal cash flows
inputs_detail.derivation: 0.54 x 13.76% + 0.46 x 9.0% = 7.43% + 4.14% = 11.57%, not rounded. Weights: market equity $48.8B (551.5M x $88.57) against ~$42B gross debt ($35.55B + $4.2B convert + Q3 draws). Round 1's arithmetic error (12.1% stated vs 12.4% computed) and its 21% shield are removed.
About nominal GDP and below the 5.3% 10-yr yield. The terminal FCF carries growth capex (2.6x x g) plus steady-state replacement.

Supervisor's round-2 correction: put capex on one basis. Round 2 took the FY26 accrual guide ($37B) less H1 cash PP&E purchases ($14.1B). On an accrual basis, H1 additions were ~$18.7B (gross PP&E $33.9B -> $52.6B, 10-Q), so H2-26 accrual capex is ~$18.3B (Q3 $12.5B guide, Q4 ~$5.8B), not $22.9B. That lowers financial net debt to ~$56.1B. But the 10-Q shows $9.8B of H1 non-cash PP&E additions 'including OEM financed additions' that are later reclassified to debt, and accrued purchases of $5.5B at Jun-30. I add ~$5.5B of these OEM-financed capex liabilities as debt-like, for $61.6B (vs $60.7B in round 2; supervisor ~$61B +/- $4B). The rest of the bridge is unchanged: Jun-30 principal $35.55B less $6.92B cash, the convert netted apart from the $0.57B capped call, Q1-Q3'27 capex $22.8B, interest ~8.5-9%, less ~$3.0B ATM proceeds. Round 4 adds the off-balance-sheet JV commitments (JV-2: $1.7B committed less $479M carried; NJ JV: ~$0.10B remaining + 50% of a $95M guarantee; 10-Q Q2-26, flag F5) and nets the NJ EDA Kenilworth credit (up to $250M, p 0.85, PV).

551.5M Class A+B (10-Q cover / StockAnalysis) + 24M options (10-Q: outstanding at Jun-30-26, $1.84 avg strike, so fully dilutive) + ~20M from the 29M unvested RSUs (10-Q), net of tax withholding + 35M ATM shares (8-K 9/17) = ~630M. The 2033 converts ($97.85) are excluded below conversion; the capped call offsets dilution up to $199.70.

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate on RPO-backed cash flows (IG counterparties)
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchored on CoreWeave's own secured cost against a Meta (Aa3/AA-) contract: DDTL 4.0, rated A3, SOFR+2.25%, ~5.9% fixed, 90% LTC. Add ~110bp for completion/operating risk and the 10% equity slice (0.9 x 5.9% + 0.1 x ~15% = 6.8%, rounded up). Applies to Meta (~$34B), NVIDIA's $6.3B backstop (Aa1/AA) and an assumed 40% of the ~$33B unnamed remainder (Microsoft Aaa is a legacy customer; judgment).

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate on RPO-backed cash flows (weaker counterparties)
inputs_detail.derivation: Spread ladder of CoreWeave's own secured debt: OpenAI-backed DDTL 3.0 at S+400 (~7.9%), mixed-contract DDTL 5.0 at S+450, short-dated DDTL 5.5 at S+550, unsecured 9-9.75%. Asset rate = debt cost + ~110bp. Jane Street is split-rated (Fitch BBB-, Moody's Ba1, S&P BB), so it sits between IG and OpenAI. All are below the 11.6% WACC and above the IG rate, as the brief requires.

inputs_detail.value: IG 52%, Jane Street 6%, OpenAI + Anthropic 23%, other 19% of $77.1B remaining at 2027-10-01
inputs_detail.derivation: $103.7B RPO at 6/30/26 (10-Q). Named: Meta $35.2B (two orders), OpenAI $22.4B less ~$3-4B recognised, NVIDIA $6.3B, Jane Street $6B, Anthropic ~$5B (analyst est.). Remaining ~$33B unnamed; 40% assumed IG. Same mix applied across the schedule (the 2030-32 tail likely skews more to Meta/NVIDIA, so this is conservative).

Evidence of slippage: Helios II slipped ~1 yr, DDTL 3.0 covenants pushed out 'to align with delivery schedule', Poolside Horizon terminated. Leased sites with signed leases and funded landlords 0.90-0.95; self-builds and new markets 0.70-0.85. Failure case ~0 because CoreWeave pays no rent or fit-out on undelivered shells.

inputs_detail.value: PIPE-LAND 0.65; residual to 8 GW path (NVIDIA framework overlap) 0.35
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 call: 4.2 GW contracted plus >1.5 GW powered land/options/LOIs 'puts you close to about 6 GW' toward >8 GW by 2030. The first 1.4 GW has identified land and power (0.65); the rest needs new sites, contracts and funding at 9-10% corporate debt costs (0.35). Valued net of growth capex at WACC: negative at k 2.6 (-$11.0 and -$4.2/sh).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Oct-27 NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) adj. EBITDA $19.1B x 6.0x = $114.6B EV, less $63.0B net debt (incl. $1.37B JV commitments) = $51.6B, over 630M shares = $81.9

inputs_detail.derivation: Cohort model NTM on the site-bucketed path (2028 nameplate $35.3B vs $38B in round 3, because contracted-not-energized sites are weighted by delivery probability and the 2028 average lines up with >3 GW at YE27 and ~4 GW at YE28 at $10-11M/MW). Model NTM $18.9B plus the same +$0.24B round-3 adjustment for the July ~25% price increase on new contracts.

Today: equity $48.8B + corrected net debt ~$39.5B (convert proceeds netted) = $88.3B EV. NTM EBITDA is $13.6B: Q4'26 $2.7B (FY guide implies ~$4.6B revenue) plus Q1-Q3'27 $10.9B (59% of $18.4B on the consensus path). That gives ~6.5x now. Trimmed to 6.0x because growth slows from ~105% to ~44% by the horizon. Round 3 keeps 6.0x. The GPU-life research argues EBITDA overstates owner earnings (refresh capex every ~6 yrs), but the market already trades at ~6.5x with this debate public (Burry, Kerrisdale), and spot rents are rising, so the research gives no clean reason to move the horizon multiple.
$61.6B (round 3) + $1.37B JV commitments (flag F5). The NJ EDA credit is left out of the multiple leg.
Same as the DCF

bear.story: Rubin ramps through 2027 and Hopper/Blackwell rents start the post-successor slide, so recontracts on the 2023-24 cohorts disappoint. Site deliveries slip further (Helios II past H1-27, Indonesia past 2028, Hammond deferred), and funding gets dearer (CDS back past ~855bp), needing equity beyond the 35M ATM. ~4.75x NTM EBITDA of ~$17.6B = $84B EV, less ~$64.4B net debt incl. JV commitments, over ~650M shares = ~$30.

base.story: Contracted sites deliver broadly on time (>3 GW active at YE27), ~$26B 2027 revenue and ~59% adj. margin; spot rents stay firm, but the market keeps discounting GPU-life risk and gives no credit to the uncontracted pipeline. ~5.6x NTM EBITDA of $19.8B (between the probability-weighted $19.1B and full delivery) = $111B EV, less $63.0B, over 630M shares = ~$76.

bull.story: The shortage persists (A100s under contract into 2029, flat compute futures curve), PIPE-LAND converts into IG-backed contracts financed at DDTL 4.0-style rates, and the market credits a 7-8 yr life. 2027 revenue beats ($28-30B), CDS tightens toward ~450bp. ~7.3x NTM EBITDA of ~$21.8B = $159B EV, less ~$60B net debt, over ~650M shares = ~$152.

thesis_break_reason: $42 (was $45) is ~31% below the 52-week low of $60.55. Same logic as before: it corresponds to ~4.9x 2027 EBITDA of $15.5B on ~$49.4B of early-2027 net debt, now including the $1.37B of JV commitments that round 3 left out (worth ~$2.2/sh), plus 630M shares = ~$42. A sustained trade there would most likely mean a failed or very expensive debt raise, a DDTL covenant problem, a top-customer cut, recontract prices collapsing, or a cluster of site failures (Helios II, PF1-B3, Lancaster and Kenilworth all due in 2027). New break signals in round 4: a second contracted site going the way of Poolside Horizon, or any DDTL 4.0 draw being refused at customer acceptance.

catalysts.event: CME/Silicon Data compute futures launch: the first exchange forward curve for GPU-hour prices (a steep backwardation would price the post-successor decay in the DCF)
ATM program share sales (up to 35M shares) and continuing insider Form 144 / Form 4 sales
Hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (Alphabet/Meta ~Oct 28, Amazon ~Oct 29, Microsoft late Oct; estimated dates) and the FOMC on Oct 27-28
CoreWeave Q3 2026 results: guide was revenue $3.45-3.6B, adj. op income $200-260M, capex $11.5-13.5B; update to backlog and contracted power
NVIDIA FQ3 results and Vera Rubin ramp commentary

GPU rental and resale indices (Ornn OCPI, Silicon Data, SemiAnalysis, CCIR used prices) and any CoreWeave disclosure of recontract pricing on 2023-24 H100 cohorts: the DCF now hinges on the post-contract price path (shortage vs normalising vs glut)
DDTL 5.5 draw window closes (per Cape Fear Advisors); end-2026 active power target >1.85 GW and exit ARR $18.5-19.5B
Q4 2026 results and first FY2027 guidance (revenue, capex, interest)
$6.18B of debt principal due in 2027; refinancing terms vs 9-9.75% senior notes
2033 converts become convertible if the stock holds >=130% of $97.85 (~$127); dilution offset by capped call up to $199.70
Site energizations inside the >1.85 GW YE26 guide: Cheyenne B1 (88 MW), eStruxture CAL-3, DataVita DV1, Dalton Phase 2 first halls
Contracted site deliveries: Galaxy Helios II (260 MW, already slipped once), Kenilworth (first owned self-build), Bell Saskatchewan, Polaris Forge 1 third building (mid-2027), Lancaster (summer 2027)
DDTL 4.0 draw window ends (Meta-backed, ~5.9%): the scale of IG contract financing sets the contracted discount rate
DDTL 3.0 (OpenAI-backed) DSCR test starts after its deferral

key_uncertainties: Post-contract GPU pricing is still the swing factor: at k 2.6x and a 6-yr life the split-rate DCF runs from -$20 (shortage persists) to -$62 (glut) per share; positive only with a 7+ yr life in the shortage regime or k <= 2.3x

Capital intensity: each 0.1x of k is worth ~$15/sh at a 6-yr life. The uncontracted pipeline is value-negative at k 2.6 and WACC (-$15/sh): building more only helps if new capacity is signed with IG customers and financed near DDTL 4.0 rates

Site delivery: 2.4 GW of contracted-not-energized capacity is weighted at an average p 0.86 (Helios II slipped a year, Poolside terminated); each 10 pts of delivery probability is worth ~$3.6/sh in the DCF and more in the EBITDA multiple
Counterparty mix of the RPO: the split rate adds only $3.2/sh because just $77B of signed contracts remain at Oct-27 and ~42% of it is unrated or weak (OpenAI, Anthropic, short-dated)
Funding cost and access: net debt ~$63B incl. JV commitments by Oct-27; each $5B is ~$8/sh; CDS has swung 452-855bp in 2026
Dilution (35M ATM, options, RSUs, 2033 converts above $97.85) and AI-capex sentiment for a 93%-vol stock: the 12-month price is driven by the EBITDA multiple, not the DCF
reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage + split discounting). (1) Sites: I replaced the top-down 8 GW x $7M/MW path with a site-bucketed one built from sites.md. Every one of the 45 inventory rows is counted once: 14 named energized sites (990 MW) + Cheyenne + a 772 MW undisclosed-MW pool make up the 1.85 GW YE26 base at $10M/MW-yr. The contracted-not-energized 2,435 MW (4.2 GW + Niagara's definitive 85 MW lease, which post-dates the LOI-excluding 4.2 GW, less E) is weighted by each site's delivery probability (expected 2,098 MW) at $11M/MW-yr. PIPE-LAND (1,415 MW after moving Niagara out) has p 0.65 and the residual to the round-3 $76B path has p 0.35, both net of growth capex at WACC. Poolside and the CORZ merger are removed. JV commitments ($1.37B) go into net debt, and their capacity sits in the C pool rather than being counted again. Landlord leases are CoreWeave outflows, already in the 30% capacity cost (observed $1.44-2.2M/MW-yr + power ~ $2.6-2.8M vs $3.0-3.3M modelled). Central EV split: energized $41.7/sh, contracted $31.0/sh, pipeline -$15.2/sh. (2) Discounting: only cash flows inside signed contracts get the lower rate, which caps them at the $77.1B of RPO left at Oct-27. By counterparty: IG 7.0% (DDTL 4.0 anchor), Jane Street 8.0%, OpenAI/Anthropic 9.0%, other 10.0% (PV-equivalent 8.06%). That adds +$2.0B, $3.2/sh, close to the supervisor's +0.1-0.15 per $ of run-rate estimate. DCF: floored expectation $0.76 single-rate -> $1.0 split (round 3 $1.5); unfloored central -$53 -> -$45.5 single -> -$42.3 split. The floored number fell slightly because a smaller pipeline cuts the k 2.3 shortage cell, the only one with real upside. EV/EBITDA: NTM $20.3B -> $19.1B (probability-weighted 2028) and net debt +$1.4B -> $81.9. Fair value $49 -> $41.5. Ladder: the multiple leg fell ~14%, but the 12-month price still runs on sentiment and spot GPU rents, so I move the core median $83 -> $80 and the distress weight 11% -> 11.5% (median $24); P(>=89) 0.413 -> 0.392. Scenarios: bear $30/0.30, base $76/0.46, bull $152/0.24. Thesis break $45 -> $42 for the JV debt. The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Research: one search (Niagara definitive lease confirmed, MW not restated); RPO buckets and the 4.2 GW LOI exclusion re-read in the 10-Q and the Q2 transcript.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: 85% of each cohort at the contract price for the 5-yr term (15% on the market path from day one); after that, price relative to the original contract by age: shortage (w 0.30) 1.00, 1.00, 0.97, 0.95, 0.93, 0.90, 0.86, 0.82; normalising (w 0.50) 1.00, 1.00, 0.88, 0.78, 0.70, 0.64, 0.59, 0.54, 0.50; glut (w 0.20) 1.00, 1.00, 0.80, 0.65, 0.57, 0.52, 0.48, 0.44; times 0.92 relative utilisation (0.95 / 0.90). Steep in the ~2 yrs after the next generation ships, then flat. The cash tail runs while price x 0.88 > 30% capacity cost (~9 yrs normalising). Tech is refreshed at the economic life with salvage of 14 / 10 / 7% of tech cost at 5 / 6 / 7 yrs.
gpu_life.note: Per share at 2027-10-01, split-rate DCF on the round-4 site-bucketed path: the expectation over regimes and k (2.3 / 2.6 / 2.7 at 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.25), each cell floored at zero; 8 yrs $6.3. Single-rate: $0.0 / $0.76 / $2.1 / $5.4. Unfloored at k 2.6, regime-weighted, split: -$56.8 (5 yrs), -$42.3 (6), -$31.7 (7), -$25.5 (8). At 6 yrs by regime: shortage -$20, normalising -$48, glut -$62. The round-3 approach is kept: contract price for the 5-yr term, a declining re-lease path, refresh capex consistent with life. The fact-check confirms CoreWeave's 6-yr book life (FY25 10-K), Nebius 5 and IREN 5; salvage is 'not disclosed' rather than 'zero', and my 10% (CCIR-based) stands. The split rate touches only signed-contract years, so it barely changes the life sensitivity.

discounting.basis: Contracted = net cash flow (58% EBITDA margin less SBC and tax) on the $77.1B of RPO left at 2027-10-01, scheduled per the 10-Q buckets (41% months 1-24, 39% months 25-48, 20% months 49-78 from 6/30/26). Rates by counterparty: IG 52% (Meta Aa3, NVIDIA Aa1 backstop, an assumed 40% of the unnamed rest) at 7.0%, anchored on DDTL 4.0, CoreWeave's Meta-backed non-recourse loan rated A3 at ~5.9% fixed, plus ~110bp for completion/operating risk and the equity slice; Jane Street (BBB-/Ba1/BB) 6% at 8.0%; OpenAI + Anthropic (unrated; DDTL 3.0 at S+400) 23% at 9.0%; other/short-dated (DDTL 5.0/5.5 at S+450/550) 19% at 10.0%. 8.06% is the single rate with the same PV. The capex still to come on RPO capacity (~$5B) is also discounted at the contracted rate. Uncontracted: post-contract years, unsigned future contracts (including the unsold share of contracted-power sites), refresh cohorts, pipeline and terminal value stay at the 11.6% WACC. Split uplift +$2.0B EV (+$3.2/sh). Values are the floored regime x k expectations at a 6-yr life; unfloored central -$45.5 single vs -$42.3 split. Site reconciliation (central: k 2.6, 6 yrs, regime-weighted, split): 13 named energized sites $21.8 + Dalton (P1 energized + P2 contracted) $2.65 + Cheyenne $1.9 + energized undisclosed-MW pool $17.4 + 8 named contracted sites $19.5 (incl. $0.25 Kenilworth EDA credit) + unattributed contracted pool $9.6 + pipeline -$15.2 = $57.7/sh EV; less net debt $97.8 and JV commitments $2.2 = -$42.3/sh.
